solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dead month at the end of the year went slowly (8)

blocks.clueFragment: month at the end of the year
blocks.note: DEC is the calendar abbreviation for December, the last month
to ease is to move slowly and carefully, as in 'eased into the parking space'

explanation.surface: A gloomy note about the year dragging to a close in a dead December.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface runs 'Dead month' together as one idea, but 'Dead' stands alone as the definition and the month is only DEC.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceased means no longer living, which is exactly dead.

clue.text: The best part of A-level I teach (5)

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters taken from the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of 'level' through 'I' into the start of 'teach'

explanation.surface: A teacher boasting that their A-level class is the highlight of the job.
explanation.walkthrough: A-levels are the exams English students sit at about 18. The hyphen and the word breaks are ignored, so the answer runs across three words.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite of a group is its best part, the pick of the bunch.

clue.text: What holds fishing line that’s run out for fish (3)

indicators.note: run is out, so its letter R leaves the word

blocks.note: an angler's line is wound on a reel
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An angler's spool empties of line just as the fish takes the bait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run out' looks like a cricket dismissal or line paying off the reel; here run means only R, and out tells it to leave REEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An eel is a long snake-like fish.

clue.text: Perhaps rose a short time in submarine (5)

indicators.note: the short time goes inside the submarine

blocks.note: HR is the short form of hour
sub is the everyday short word for a submarine

explanation.surface: Someone who perhaps rose to the surface after a short spell in a submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps rose' reads as a verb, someone getting up; it is the flower, a shrub, with 'perhaps' warning that a rose is only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose bush is one kind of shrub, a woody plant smaller than a tree.

clue.text: Lower deck is holding record (7)

indicators.note: the deck word holds the record inside it

blocks.note: to deck or dress something is to adorn it, as in 'decked with flags'
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A ship's lower deck is where the log of the voyage is kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower deck' reads as part of a ship; 'Lower' is the verb, and deck means adorn, not a floor.
explanation.definitionFit: To depress something is to push it down, to lower it.

clue.text: Dread musical ability going after fever’s onset (4)

indicators.note: the musical ability is placed after the F
the onset of fever is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of fever
someone with an ear for music can pick out tunes

explanation.surface: A musician terrified that a fever will rob them of their talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dread' could be an adjective here, but it is the noun, matching FEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: dread as a noun is the deep fear of something to come.

clue.text: Anticipate topping everything with wood (9)

indicators.note: in a down answer, the wood sits on top of everything

blocks.note: a forest is a large wood
all = everything

explanation.surface: Guessing ahead of time what a cake topping of wood might taste like.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads the parts in reverse: 'topping everything with wood' means wood goes above everything, so FOREST comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to act in anticipation of something so as to prevent it.

clue.text: Gold — something generating interest — is a favourable sign (7)

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
spice is what adds interest or excitement, as in 'variety is the spice of life'

explanation.surface: A banker hails gold as a lucky omen because it earns interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interest' suggests money earned on savings, pointing to a bank; here it means excitement, which spice supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: An auspice is an omen, especially a favourable one, as in 'auspicious'.

clue.text: Call back youth around one (4)

indicators.note: the whole thing is written backwards
the youth goes around the one

blocks.note: a lad is a boy or young man
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Telling someone to ring back a young man about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call back' looks like one instruction, to return a phone call, but only 'Call' is the definition; 'back' turns LAID round.
explanation.definitionFit: Call in the telephone sense: you ring a number by keying or turning the dial.

clue.text: Word differently with hearers confused about page (8)

indicators.note: the letters of hearers are mixed up
the mixed letters go around the page

blocks.note: HEARERS with its letters rearranged
p is the standard abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: Rewording something because the listeners got muddled over a page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Word' opens the clue looking like a noun; it is the verb, to put into words, so 'Word differently' is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To rephrase is to put something in different words.

clue.text: Permit the growing of crops that can be sustained (8)

blocks.note: the verb read loosely as 'let be', allowing something to exist
arable describes farmland ploughed for crops

explanation.surface: A farming rule on whether a field may be planted with crops that will last.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half works best as a whole phrase: land that permits the growing of crops is land that will be arable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bearable can be endured, sustained without giving way.

clue.text: Prepare servant verbally for immediate employment (5-4)

indicators.note: the servant word is spoken, so its sound is written a different way

blocks.note: to ready something is to prepare it
a maid is a female servant; MAID and MADE sound the same

explanation.surface: Getting a servant ready to start work straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employment' suggests a job for the servant, but it means use: something ready-made can be used at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready-made goods are made in advance and available for immediate use.

clue.text: Small child’s slide (4)

blocks.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a kid is a child; the 's is read as 'is', joining the parts

explanation.surface: A little one's playground slide.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'slide' a playground toy; it is slipping out of control.
explanation.definitionFit: A skid is a sliding, uncontrolled slip, as of a car on ice.

clue.text: March is leaving Shangri-La, say (6)

indicators.note: IS departs from the word for Shangri-La

blocks.note: Shangri-La is the paradise of James Hilton's novel Lost Horizon; 'say' marks it as an example
the letters to remove, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone heading off from a mythical Himalayan paradise in the month of March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' at the start looks like the month because of its capital; it is the verb, a procession.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the noun sense: troops on parade march past in formation.

clue.text: Disparaging area public transport one has (7)

blocks.note: A is the standard abbreviation for area
a bus is public transport
I is the Roman numeral for one
've is the contracted form of have, as in I've

explanation.surface: A commuter grumbling rudely about the local buses.
explanation.walkthrough: The contraction is the hard part: 'one has' reads as I'VE, giving the last three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: language that belittles or insults someone is both.

clue.text: Train like a former Times reporter? (7)

blocks.note: a fast train making few stops
EX = former, and reporters are collectively the press

explanation.surface: A journalist who has left The Times, compared to a train.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsy: a former reporter is ex-press, once a member of the press, and The Times is where this clue is printed.
explanation.definitionFit: An express is a fast train making few stops.

clue.text: Upset fish in tin (6)

indicators.note: the fish sits inside the tin symbol

blocks.note: hake is a sea fish
Sn is the chemical symbol for tin

explanation.surface: Someone upset to find a fish in a tin, a can of sardines gone wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tin' suggests a can of fish, but it is the metal, symbol Sn.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaken means upset or disturbed, as after a shock.

clue.text: Splash out on grabbing ring float (4)

indicators.note: the spending word grabs the ring and holds it inside

blocks.note: to splash out on something is to spend money buying it
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Treating yourself to a ring-shaped inflatable for the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: The splash and the ring both suggest water and a rubber ring, which a buoy nearly is, but splash out means spend.
explanation.definitionFit: A buoy is a float, moored in water as a marker.

clue.text: Cruel coalmine I bar (8)

blocks.note: a pit is a coalmine
taken as written
bar and less both mean except, as in 'all bar one'

explanation.surface: A miner complaining that the pit refuses them entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' reads as a verb (I bar) or a pub; it is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitiless means showing no pity, cruel.

clue.text: Teacher taking up harmful alcohol? That’s not good (5)

indicators.note: in a down answer, up turns the word so it reads bottom to top
the good is not there, so its letter leaves

blocks.note: rotgut is cheap, harmful liquor
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A teacher taking up drinking bad booze, which is not a good idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's not good' reads as a verdict on the drinking; it is the instruction to remove G from ROTGUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, though usually for someone teaching one pupil or a small group.

clue.text: Laugh at son over trite humour (5)

indicators.note: in a down answer, the son sits above the humour

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for son in family trees
corn is stale, corny humour

explanation.surface: Mocking a son for his dad-joke sense of humour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' could mean about, but here it places S on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A near-synonym: mocking laughter is one way of showing contempt for someone.

clue.text: Line one item of clothing not having right tough fibre (8)

indicators.note: the clothing word does without its R

blocks.note: L is the standard abbreviation for line
I is the Roman numeral for one
a garment is an item of clothing
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Lining a garment with a tough fibre instead of the right material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' at the start looks like a verb, to line clothes; it is only L.
explanation.definitionFit: A ligament is a band of tough fibrous tissue joining bones.

clue.text: Embarrassing mistake docking bird’s tail (4)

indicators.note: to dock an animal is to cut off its tail
the tail of the bird is its last letter

blocks.note: a booby is a tropical seabird
last letter of BOOBY

explanation.surface: A clumsy groom's gaffe in cutting a bird's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: A boob is British slang for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British usage: a silly blunder that makes you look foolish.

clue.text: Bird driving another away in scrap (3)

indicators.note: one bird drives another out
the second bird goes away, leaving the rest

blocks.note: a bittern is a marsh bird of the heron family
a tern is another bird, a seabird

explanation.surface: One bird chasing another off during a squabble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' suggests the fight in the surface; it means a small piece. The second bird sits inside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean a small leftover piece, as in 'a scrap of paper'.

clue.text: Charge including time for outdoor function (4)

indicators.note: the charge includes the time inside it

blocks.note: a fee is a charge
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An entry fee that covers time at an open-air event.
explanation.walkthrough: A fete is a British outdoor fair, often to raise money, with stalls and games.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor festive event, a function held in the open air.

clue.text: Prison officer reported very little inspection (8)

indicators.note: the prison officer word is spoken, so only its sound counts

blocks.note: screw is British slang for a prison warder
tiny = very little

explanation.surface: A warder said to have done very little checking of the cells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reported' looks like it belongs to the officer filing a report; it only asks for the sound of SCREW.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a careful, searching examination of something.
